original_value: In the last months, the market for personal wearable devices has been booming significantly, and, in particular, smartwatches are starting to assume a fundamental role in the Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) arena as well as in the more general Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, by acting both as sensitive data sources and as user identity proxies. These new roles, complementing the more traditional personal assistance and telemetry/tracking ones, open new perspectives in their integration in complex IoT-based critical infrastructures such as e-payment, health care monitoring, and emergency systems, as well as in their usage as remote control facilities in smart services. Users can access their IoT devices at any time from any place through smartwatches. We argue that this new scenario calls for a strengthened and more resilient authentication of users on these devices, despite their limitations in terms of dimensions and hardware constraints that may considerably affect the usability of security mechanisms. In this article, we present an innovative authentication scheme targeted at smartwatches, namely CirclePIN, that provides both resilience to most common attacks and a high level of usability in tests with real users.

result.paraphrase: Recently, the personal wearable device market has been growing rapidly, and smartwatches in particular are taking on a key role in the Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) space and in the broader Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem by serving both as sensitive data sources and as proxies for user identity. Alongside their more traditional personal-assistance and telemetry/tracking functions, these new roles create fresh opportunities for integration into complex IoT-based critical infrastructures such as e-payment, health care monitoring, and emergency systems, as well as for use as remote-control tools in smart services. Through smartwatches, users can reach their IoT devices anytime and from anywhere. We contend that this situation requires stronger, more resilient user authentication on these devices, even though their limited size and hardware constraints can significantly reduce the usability of security mechanisms. In this article, we introduce CirclePIN, an innovative smartwatch authentication scheme that delivers resilience against most common attacks while maintaining a high level of usability in tests with real users.
